name: volume-slider-mirrors-core
description: Two real Quick volume drags keep the visible slider and mpv session synchronized across their 0..1 and 0..100 scales.

steps.note: Moved DOWN first. Two steps in opposite directions are what make this a synchronisation check: a single point could agree by coincidence with a volume the player happened to start at.
Bounded settles so the core's answer is observable after each write. The synchronisation itself is asserted, never timed.

assertions.note: The final mpv level is the slider's 0.8 input scaled to 80.
The Quick volume rail's read-only value reports the controller's final 0.8 level.

The level written one step earlier, so a core that froze at the first write cannot pass by holding a stale-but-matching value. Deliberately an exact compare: the runner reads tolerance only under approximately (compareValues in ProbeRunner.cpp), so a tolerance here would be silently ignored and would not print in the report line. Exact is also the stronger claim - it rejects the precise stale value rather than a band around it.
